rename.from: JUnit 5 Assumptions do not work in @BeforeAll annotated methods
rename.to: JUnit Jupiter Assumptions do not work in @BeforeAll methods

body:
Thanks for bringing this to our attention!

I have confirmed that this is in fact a _bug_.

Specifically, it's a bug in the internals of the `HierarchicalTestEngine`, and the bug exists currently on the `master` branch.

Note that executing the example `AssumptionTestJUnit4` test class on the JUnit Platform via the `VintageTestEngine` also results in a failure instead of the test class being skipped.
I believe the _fix_ for this bug must go into `org.junit.platform.engine.support.hierarchical.NodeTestTask.executeRecursively()` (on `master`).
Or perhaps proper handling of "aborting exceptions" in `org.junit.platform.engine.support.hierarchical.NodeTestTask.reportCompletion()` would be the better place for such a fix.
We'll likely need to _open up_ `org.junit.platform.engine.support.hierarchical.ThrowableCollector.hasAbortedExecution(Throwable)` so that it can be queried from within `reportCompletion()`.

@jkarshin, how are you executing those tests?

Are you seeing the failure in **Eclipse IDE** by any chance?

**Update**:

This sounds like a known [bug in Eclipse IDE](https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=536005) which is marked as resolved for Eclipse 4.9 M2.

Since we have tests in place that verify support for failed assumptions in _before all_ callback methods, I am therefore inclined to close this issue as "works as designed", but I am awaiting a confirmation from @jkarshin that the behavior was noticed in a version of Eclipse IDE prior to version 4.9 M2.

@jkarshin, since you stated "The following JUnit4 test (run against the JUnit4 test runner)", I assume you are referring to the _Eclipse JUnit 4 Test Runner_, but I'd still appreciate a confirmation from you. 😉

@sbrannen Thanks for the quick reply! Yes, I was running these tests through Eclipse 4.8.0.

I'll update my Eclipse and try the test again on Monday.

You're welcome, and thanks for the feedback.

By the way, I just verified the expected behavior in the latest version of Eclipse:

> Eclipse IDE for Java Developers
> Version: 2018-09 (4.9.0)
> Build id: 20180917-1800
> OS: Mac OS X, v.10.13.6, x86_64 / cocoa
> Java version: 11

The bug has in fact been fixed in Eclipse, and I am therefore closing this issue.
